mappings.note: Picks the saturated formulae out of five. Homologous-series membership from the general formula, LO-4.
Functional group in CH3CH2CH2COOH (carboxyl). LO-4 verbatim.
Names given compounds. Nomenclature, LO-4.
Identifies functional groups in given compounds. LO-4.
Writes IUPAC names. Nomenclature, LO-4.
Draws the structural formulae of the C3H6O isomers. The isomer clause of C 1.3-LO-4; no naming is asked, so not C 1.1-LO-4.
Ethene to ethanol by acid-catalysed hydration, with the equation. Preparation of ethanol, LO-8.
Defines a homologous series and applies it to three formulae. LO-4.
The two features of carbon behind the number of its compounds. LO-3 restated.
Petrol versus kerosene as a fuel -- cleaner, more complete combustion. Combustion has no outcome in this frame; cited at the C 1.3 competency.
Draws the aldehyde and ketone of C3H6O and states they are isomers (C 1.3-LO-4), and also asks for their names (C 1.1-LO-4).
Warm ethanol with alkaline KMnO4: the colour change, the reason and the product. Oxidation of ethanol, LO-8.
Naming the aldehyde from methane and the ketone from butane is LO-4; the third part, the product of oxidising ethanol, is LO-8.
IUPAC names for the two C3H6O isomers (LO-4 of C 1.1) plus the structure of the second one (C 1.3-LO-4).

C2H4O2 that smells pleasant and fails both acid tests must be the ester, not ethanoic acid -- the reasoning is entirely about ethanoic acid's properties (LO-8); the structural formula asked for is C 1.3-LO-4.
Acetic acid on solid X gives a gas that turns lime water milky, so X is a carbonate. A reaction of ethanoic acid, LO-8.
Oxidation of C2H6O by alkaline KMnO4. The reaction is the ethanol oxidation of LO-8. (The stem's formulae do not add up -- see defect list.)
Names the functional group in four written formulae. LO-4 verbatim.
(a) Draw ethanoic acid and butanone -- C 1.3-LO-4. (b) Why ethanol to ethanoic acid is oxidation -- LO-8.
What esters are, how they form and their uses. Esterification, LO-8.
Naming two '-oic acid' compounds is LO-4; the balanced reaction of one with sodium hydroxide is a reaction of a carboxylic acid, LO-8.
The two-carbon '-ol' compound is ethanol; heating with excess conc. H2SO4 dehydrates it. A reaction of ethanol, LO-8.
Ethanol dehydrated to ethene and the role of conc. H2SO4 -- LO-8. Part (a) also asks for the names of A, B and C, which is LO-4.
Ethanol from wine oxidised to the ethanoic acid of vinegar, then esterified -- all three LO-8 reactions; the structural formulae demanded add C 1.3-LO-4.
Three separate tests, one per outcome: ethane versus ethene is unsaturation (LO-4), ethanol versus ethanoic acid is LO-8, and soap versus detergent in hard water is LO-9.
Part (a) is the homologous series and its characteristics (LO-4); parts (b) and (c) are the KMnO4 oxidation of ethanol and telling an alcohol from an acid (LO-8).
(a) and (b) are the weak ionisation and carbonate reaction of ethanoic acid (LO-8); (c) asks for the principle of soap's cleansing action (LO-9).
Esterification versus saponification, then an activity making an ester. LO-8 names both reactions.
Alkaline hydrolysis of a C4H8O2 ester and what saponification means -- LO-8; the structural formula of the ester is C 1.3-LO-4.
C3H6 rather than C3H8 adds, because it is unsaturated (LO-4); the vegetable-ghee equation is a hydrogenation, cited at C 1.3 as the frame has no addition-reaction outcome.
Percentage of carbon in the crust. Abundance has no outcome in this frame -- LO-3 is tetravalency and catenation -- so the competency is cited, as for 85342.

Which property ionic compounds lack, asked here as the foil to covalent carbon compounds. Ionic bonding has no learning outcome in this chapter's frame, so the C 1.1 competency on compound formation is cited.
Electronic configuration of carbon (2,4) -- the four valence electrons that make it tetravalent. LO-3.
Carbon-based compounds are called organic compounds. The class of compounds LO-3 explains the size of.
Carbon compounds are covalently bonded. Covalency follows from tetravalency, LO-3.
The noble gas with two outer electrons (helium). Periodic classification, C 1.1; neither carbon LO applies.
Atomic number of chlorine. Atomic structure and the Periodic Table, C 1.1; not a carbon outcome.
Element with six electrons in the L shell (oxygen). Configuration and Periodic Table placement, C 1.1.
Bond in N2. Not a carbon compound, so the carbon-specific C 1.3-LO-4 does not apply; competency cited.
Formula of ammonia. A non-carbon molecule represented by symbols -- C 1.3 competency, not the carbon-restricted LO-4.
A shared electron pair is a covalent bond. Stated generally, but it is the bonding idea LO-3 builds carbon's tetravalency on; no other code is nearer.
Covalent compounds conduct poorly. A consequence of the covalent bonding LO-3 addresses.
The rigid three-dimensional allotrope where each carbon makes four bonds -- diamond. Tetravalency made visible, LO-3.
C60 is fullerene. Allotropy of carbon, under LO-3.
The conducting allotrope, graphite. Allotropy of carbon, LO-3.
Carbon bonding to carbon is catenation. LO-3's catenation clause.
Single-bonded carbon compounds are saturated. Series classification, LO-4.
Double or triple bonds mean unsaturated. Series classification, LO-4.
What methane is -- the first saturated hydrocarbon. Series membership, LO-4.
Methane has four hydrogens. The count is carbon's tetravalency, LO-3, rather than a drawn structure.
C3H8 is propane. Naming within the alkane series, LO-4.
C2H2 is ethyne. Naming within the alkyne series, LO-4.
Formula of hexane. Applying the alkane general formula, LO-4.
Same molecular formula, different structures = isomers. The isomer clause of C 1.3-LO-4.
Compounds of carbon and hydrogen only are hydrocarbons. Family classification, LO-4.
The alcohol functional group (-OH). LO-4 verbatim.
CH3OH is methanol. Naming from the functional group, LO-4.
General formula of the alkanes. Homologous series, LO-4.
General formula of the alkenes. Homologous series, LO-4.
General formula of the alkynes. Homologous series, LO-4.
